key_insight: Thin-film barium titanate (BTO) retains strong piezoelectricity from room temperature down to millikelvin, enabling high-frequency resonators with potential quantum-hardware utility.
engineering_relevance: The material offers a tunable piezoelectric platform for reconfigurable RF components and superconducting quantum circuits, with strong electromechanical coupling at microwave frequencies.
method: Fabricated SAW resonators on thin-film BTO
Measured electromechanical response from room temperature to millikelvin
Used finite-element modeling of the multi-domain microstructure to extract effective piezoelectric coefficients
evidence_signal: Devices showed k²eff = 0.14 at 5.2 GHz, operation up to 7.8 GHz, room-temperature d33eff = 53 pC/N, and millikelvin d33eff = 19 pC/N; switching occurred in 100 ns.
watch_item: Multi-domain microstructure and cryogenic integration may affect reproducibility, calibration, and device performance in scalable quantum hardware.
paper_title: Piezoelectric resonators in thin-film barium titanate from room temperature to millikelvin
